newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Primakov recovers in time for NATO talks.
newsitem.headline: Russian Primakov recovers in time for NATO talks.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov is recovering fast after an operation and will hold crucial talks over NATO enlargement with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright next week, officials said on Friday.
"He (Primakov) beats our expectations, recovering well ahead of schedule", Professor Vitaly Bashilov, who operated Primakov for a gallstone problem, told Reuters by telephone.
"Usually we would not discharge such a patient earlier than 10 to 14 days (after surgery) but Primakov may leave hospital this weekend", he added.

Primakov, 66, had to miss a scheduled meeting with Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaime Gama because of an unexpected bout of illness last Friday when he was taken to hospital and had the operation on the same day.
His absence fell on a crucial period of preparation of an accord between Russia and NATO which the two sides try to prepare for signing before a NATO summit in July.
The speedy recovery puts Primakov, Russia's key negotiator with NATO, back on track for a scheduled meeting with Albright in Moscow on May 1.

There are still unresolved differences but Russia and the Western defence alliance are racing against time to work out the Russia-NATO charter which President Boris Yeltsin hopes to sign on May 27 in Paris.
The accord is aimed at dispelling at least some of Russian security concerns over NATO's planned expansion.
Russia wants an explicit commitment from the alliance to say it will "never" station nuclear weapons on the territory of new member countries.
Moscow is also trying to prevent NATO's military infrastructure from moving towards its borders.
After talks with Albright Primakov will also meet NATO Secretary General Javier Solana on May 6 in Luxemburg, the Russian Foreign Ministry said on Friday.
